rules.statement: A store's remove operation for an owning entity must also remove every row that exists only for that owner (secrets and their key material, grants, consents, role assignments, issued tokens, and so on) in the same unit of work, rather than failing on a foreign-key violation or leaving orphaned rows.
rules.why: With Restrict foreign keys, a delete that checks only some dependents fails with a foreign-key violation (a 500 on PostgreSQL), and dependents with no foreign key silently outlive their owner as orphaned personal data.
rules.check: Look for a new or changed RemoveAsync/delete on a store that removes the owner row without also removing all of its dependent entity types, or that relies on callers to clean up dependents first.

rules.statement: Remove dependent rows explicitly through the Entity Framework change tracker so that EF orders the deletes; do not switch foreign keys to database cascade delete to achieve owner erasure.
rules.why: SQL Server refuses multiple cascade paths, the EF InMemory provider cascades only the rows it tracks, and references with no foreign key are never cascaded, so foreign keys stay Restrict and no migration is needed.
rules.check: Flag model configuration changing OnDelete to Cascade/SetNull for owner erasure, or migrations added to introduce cascades, where dependents should instead be loaded and removed in the unit of work.

rules.statement: When erasing a tenant, find the tenant-owned entity types by reading the EF model for the tenant marker interface, the same way the tenant query filter does, instead of hard-coding a list of entity sets, and also remove the secret rows that those entities reference.
rules.why: Reading the set of entity types from the model means an entity contributed by another package, such as a local account that has no foreign key to the tenant, is erased with its tenant without any change to the store.
rules.check: Look for tenant deletion code that lists specific DbSets by hand, or that skips entities that reference secrets or are referenced by identifier only.

rules.statement: When removing an entity whose identifier is global across tenants (such as a principal), remove the rows that reference it in every tenant, not only the rows visible through the current tenant's query filter.
rules.why: A principal's identifier is generated by the server and is global, and the principal may hold role assignments at nodes of another tenant, so a tenant-scoped delete would leave dangling assignments.
rules.check: Look for removal of globally identified entities, or tenant deletion, that removes cross-referencing rows (role assignments and similar) through a tenant-filtered query only.

rules.statement: An endpoint that deletes a resource must rely on the store's remove operation to remove the resource's dependents, rather than duplicating the dependent cleanup or calling a separate dependent check before the delete.
rules.why: The store's remove operation is the single place that removes what the resource owns, so any path that deletes the resource, including dynamic client deregistration, removes the same dependents.
rules.check: Look for handlers that remove secrets, tokens or grants on their own around a store RemoveAsync call, or that call a 'has dependents' check to block a delete that only authorization should block.
